answer: At the inlet of an agent marketplace, each identity must lock a stake before bidding on jobs. A verifier checks signed delivery receipts, and a proven forged receipt causes the stake to be slashed. If saffron shipments are traded at the jetty, an attacker creating a hundred bidding identities must lock a hundred stakes; splitting one stake among aliases buys no extra bidding capacity. Honest agents also bear the cost of tied-up capital.
